_comment: Gold evaluation matrix for the Sanskrit proof-checker. See scripts/build_gold_dataset.py for provenance and rationale.

cases.note: Both विद्या and लयः are independently valid words; catching this requires detecting that two valid adjacent words are more likely a wrongly-split single word/compound. No current layer attempts this (out of scope).
स्वास्थ्यम् (final म्) is itself a valid word in isolation; म् vs ं is a sandhi/style choice that depends on the following word, not decidable from this token alone.
उद्देशः is itself a distinct valid word (place/spot), not a malformed spelling of उद्देश्यः; flagging it as an error requires semantic/context judgement, not orthography.
न् vs ं before त् is a permitted orthographic variant, not an error.

रामः पिता आगच्छति is grammatically CORRECT as apposition (समानाधिकरण, २.३.४६): "Rama, the father, comes." रामस्य पिता आगच्छति ("Rama's father comes") is equally correct and means something different. Only author intent separates them, so this is a category-3 boundary, not a detection gap. Retagged from verdict=error in the closing round; see scope doc section on apposition/possession ambiguity.

अगच्छति mixes the लङ् augment अ- with a Latin-style present ending; it is not a real tiṅanta of any lakāra, so this is really a malformed-form case, not a live tense/context ambiguity. Kept as review pending a generalized tiṅanta-repair layer, not because it's ambiguous.
पुस्तकम् vs पुस्तकं before a following प is a sandhi/anusvāra writing convention (म् + labial), not an independent spelling error.

Per the spec's own caveat: an unsandhied form (रामः गच्छति) is not itself invalid Sanskrit even where रामो गच्छति is the sandhi-joined form. Modeled as 'review' (style-tier, offered not asserted), never hard 'error' — matching the documented design that unapplied external sandhi is a legitimate editorial convention.

Double space between words: formatting note, not a grammar error.
Fused tokens with no space; should not be silently mis-tokenized or flagged as an unknown word without comment.
Comma is not standard Sanskrit punctuation (danda-based); flagged as a typography note, not a grammar error.
A newline is a legitimate sentence/line break; must not itself be treated as an error.

cases.category: Proper noun homographic with a verb
cases.note: भरतः is also a Prathama dual of भृ; the real verb is गच्छन्ति.
अस्ति carries Basic Prathama readings and must keep verb status. Participle liNga agreement is a known uncovered gap (scope doc 10.3), so no flag is expected here.
Unsegmentable dvandva is review-tier; the subject-verb check must not fall through to वनं.

cases.category: Recognized subject control, accusative object present
cases.note: Control: ordinary sentence with a recognized subject is unaffected.

cases.category: Agreement error still fires with an object present
cases.note: Control: the unrecognized-subject suppression must not silence a genuine error.
-आः here is an अस्-stem (मनस्) nominative SINGULAR, not an a-stem plural. Word is unrecognized, so vacana is unconfirmable; the agreement check must decline rather than suggest सन्ति.
सुमनाः is in the lexicon as a singular; must not be read as a plural.
Control: a recognized a-stem -आः plural must keep its confirmed agreement error.
Control: the unconfirmed-vacana suppression must not reach recognized subjects.
